answers.children: Yes — Redbone Coonhounds are good with children when their determined and affectionate nature is matched with daily exercise that channels their high energy. Bred as tireless hunters of raccoons through dense swamps and forests, these medium-sized dogs with sleek builds can overwhelm small children if their boundless stamina is not burned off through long hikes or intense play. Their loyalty shows in gentle nudging for attention after activity. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: No — Redbone Coonhounds do not reliably get along with other pets because their strong prey drive leads them to chase small animals. Originally bred in the southern United States to track and tree game, this energetic hound can fixate on cats or pocket pets despite being sociable with other dogs raised alongside them. Their affectionate side emerges only after the hunting instinct is satisfied through proper outlets.
answers.exercise: Redbone Coonhounds need two hours of vigorous daily exercise such as long hikes, runs or simulated hunts across rough terrain. Without this their high energy becomes overwhelming, resulting in destructive behaviour and incessant vocalising from boredom. Developed for stamina in tracking raccoons through swamps and forests, their sleek muscular build demands sustained activity that matches the relentless drive seen in their hunting history.
answers.shedding: Yes — Redbone Coonhounds shed moderately with short smooth coats that release hair year-round onto furniture and clothing. The glossy solid red single coat lacks feathering or undercoat density so it does not mat yet still spreads noticeable fine hairs throughout the house, especially during seasonal changes. Their build as medium-sized hunters means loose coat clings less to the athletic frame than to home surfaces.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is hypoallergenic and the Redbone Coonhound is not one of those suggested for allergy sufferers. Its short smooth coat still produces dander and sheds moderate amounts of hair that can trigger reactions despite the lack of long feathering or dense undercoat. The solid red glossy texture typical of this American hunting breed offers no special advantage for those sensitive to canine allergens.
answers.training: Redbone Coonhounds are moderately easy to train because their intelligence and determination are offset by an independent streak from their history of hunting without constant direction. Bred in the United States to track raccoons through forests using their own keen nose and relentless drive, they respond to patient methods that respect their energetic temperament rather than force. Their affectionate loyalty helps once focus is achieved.
answers.lifespan: Redbone Coonhounds live 12-15 years. Their athletic build as medium-sized hunters developed for stamina in rugged southern terrain supports this range when paired with the breed's energetic nature and loyal temperament that encourage active lifestyles. Health robustness is aided by the short smooth coat that requires little maintenance and avoids the burdens of heavy feathering or dense undercoat.
answers.size: Redbone Coonhounds reach 45-70 lb and stand 21-27 in tall as adults. Their muscular yet sleek build from hunting raccoons and game across swamps and forests feels substantial without being cumbersome indoors, allowing an affectionate dog that curls at feet after activity yet still possesses the substance to cover miles of rough ground daily.
answers.barking: Yes — Redbone Coonhounds bark frequently with a deep melodious bay developed for announcing game on hunts through dense woods. This vocal trait from their origins as tireless trackers in the southern United States means they use the soulful sound to signal visitors, yard critters or pent-up energy, making them far from quiet even when affectionate and settled with family.
answers.apartment: No — Redbone Coonhounds do not suit apartment living because their high energy and frequent baying clash with confined indoor routines. Bred for relentless hunting of raccoons across forests and swamps, their determined nature and endless stamina lead to restlessness and noise when exercise falls short of the long runs or intense sessions their athletic frame requires daily.
answers.first-time: No — Redbone Coonhounds are not a good first dog because their high energy and strong prey drive demand experienced handling to prevent overwhelming owners or chasing small pets. The independent streak from their development as determined hunters in the United States challenges novices, though their affectionate loyalty rewards those who meet the breed's exercise and training needs consistently.
